fact_text: EEA nationals do not need a visa or preclearance to enter Ireland.
evidence_quote: You do not need a visa or preclearance to come to Ireland if you are a citizen of the EEA or Switzerland.

fact_text: EEA nationals may enter Ireland to take employment without obtaining an Irish employment permit.
evidence_quote: EU citizens can live and work in Ireland without a visa or work permit.

fact_text: EEA nationals living in Ireland are not required to register with Irish immigration authorities or obtain a residence card, and Ireland has no separate municipal residence-registration obligation for them.
evidence_quote: When you come to Ireland, you do not need to register with the immigration authorities and you do not need a residence card to live here.

fact_text: An EEA national must present a valid passport or national identity card to an immigration officer on arrival in Ireland.
evidence_quote: You must present a valid passport or national identity card when entering Ireland.

fact_text: An expired passport or national identity card does not satisfy Ireland's requirement for a valid identity document at entry.
evidence_quote: valid passport or national identity card

fact_text: An EEA national who becomes involuntarily unemployed after working in Ireland for more than one year retains worker status while registered as a jobseeker with the relevant employment office.
evidence_quote: he/she is in duly recorded involuntary unemployment after having been employed for more than one year and has registered as a job-seeker with the relevant employment office

fact_text: An EEA national in duly recorded involuntary unemployment during the first twelve months of employment retains worker status for at least six months if registered as a jobseeker with the relevant employment office.
evidence_quote: the status of worker shall be retained for no less than six months

entity_title: EU/EEA Social Security Coordination in Ireland
fact_text: An EEA worker is subject to the social security legislation of only one Member State at a time under Regulation (EC) No 883/2004.
evidence_quote: Persons to whom this Regulation applies shall be subject to the legislation of a single Member State only.

entity_title: EU/EEA Social Security Coordination in Ireland
fact_text: A worker posted temporarily from one Member State to Ireland may remain covered by the sending state's social security legislation when the posting is not expected to exceed 24 months and the worker is not replacing another posted person.
evidence_quote: the anticipated duration of such work does not exceed twenty-four months and that he/she is not sent to replace another person

entity_title: Ireland Proof of Address for PPSN and Banking
fact_text: An EEA professional applying for a PPS Number must provide proof of address showing their name and address and dated within the previous three months.
evidence_quote: The document must show your name and address and not be older than 3 months.

entity_title: Ireland Proof of Address for PPSN and Banking
fact_text: An EEA professional opening an Irish bank account may be required to provide proof of address, such as a recent utility bill or tenancy agreement.
evidence_quote: You may also need to provide proof of your address.
